newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CELTA SINK REAL 4-0 AS EXTREMDURA GO DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTA SINK REAL 4-0 AS EXTREMDURA GO DOWN.

text.p: Bosnian striker Vlado Gudelj handed newly-crowned Spanish champions Real Madrid their worst defeat of the season with a hat-trick in a 4-0 pounding by struggling Celta Vigo on Sunday.
Gudelj's three goals helped keep Celta in the first division, while Extremadura will be automatically relegated after going down 1-0 at Deportivo Coruna.
Rayo Vallecano lost 2-1 to Barcelona and will play off for a place in the top flight with second division Mallorca.
Real were playing their last competitive game under coach Fabio Capello, who is returning to AC Milan shortly.
Capello's side were left reeling by two early goals by Gudelj and went further behind just after the break when Juan Sanchez added the third.
There was no way back shortly afterwards for visitors Real when Fernando Hierro was sent off. Gudelj rounded off the rout in the dying minutes.
Barcelona were on the receiving end for most of their game at Rayo Vallecano. But Roger Garcia scored a late winner after Rayo's Diego Klimowizc had equalised following Hristo Stoichkov's early goal.
Extremadura, needing a win, started strongly against Deportivo.
But the first division newcomers showed the strain of an entire season spent fighting relegation and eventually went down to a goal from Aitor Beguiristain.
The game was brightened by some superb touches from Deportivo's brilliant Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo.
"It was an effort to get here (to the first division) and it's been hard trying to stay up," Extremadura coach Josu Ortuondo said.
